name: main
prose: Entry point of nfsuserd (usr.sbin/nfsuserd/nfsuserd.c:107-510; slice cut the head). It checks that the NFS subsystem is available (errx(1, ...) if not), looks up the local address (creating inet/inet6 sockets; failure is err(1, ...)), parses the arguments (-domain, -verbose, -force, -manage-gids, -usermax, -usertimeout, a server count; bad arguments call usage()), and validates the domain name: leading dots are skipped, a name of only dots or with a non-ASCII character is errx(1), and the name is lowercased with trailing dots stripped. With -force it deletes the registered port with nfssvc (errx(1) on failure). It creates the UDP socket and svcudp, registers the service (each failure is err(1)), and registers the port with nfssvc (failure prints a message, with a jail hint or an already-running hint, and exit(1)). It then sends the idname entries to the kernel with nfssvc: initialisation, up to nid_usermax groups from getgrent, and users from getpwent whose uid is not yet used (each nfssvc failure is errx(1)); in a DEBUG build these calls are replaced by printing. It frees the address info if mustfreeai is set. In a DEBUG build it then calls exit(0) and does nothing more. Otherwise it daemonizes, ignores SIGHUP/SIGINT/SIGQUIT/SIGTERM, installs cleanup_term for SIGUSR1 and SIGCHLD, and forks nfsuserdcnt children; each child runs svc_run() and exits with status 1 (after logging) if that returns; a fork failure is only logged. The master then loops forever in sigsuspend, so main does not return and ends only through a signal handler. Parts of the body between the argument parsing and the port registration were read in outline.

Reviewer rounds 15 and 17 right: in a DEBUG build main calls exit(0) after freeaddrinfo and does not daemonize or fork. Partly read: lines 123-190 (address setup) and the argument switch bodies.

name: pmc_filter_handler
prose: Filters a pmclog stream from infd to outfd (static, usr.sbin/pmc/cmd_pmc_filter.cc:196-295; lwplist/pidlist counts are at most LIST_MAX). It opens a pmclog parse state on infd (errx(EX_OSERR) if that fails), parses the process and thread name lists, and makes pass 1 over the log, copying the cpu id from the PMCLOG_TYPE_INITIALIZE event (cpuid stays uninitialised if there is none) and counting PMCALLOCATE events; if an event list was given it parses it with the cpu id. It rewinds with lseek and closes and reopens the parse state, mallocs a map of pmccount entries (errx(EX_OSERR) if NULL) and pass 2 stores the pmcid and event index of each PMCALLOCATE event. After another rewind and reopen, pass 3 records thread and process names from THR_CREATE and PROC_CREATE events and handles each event: every event that is not a CALLCHAIN is written to outfd unconditionally (pmc_log_event, which errx(EX_OSERR) on a failed write); a CALLCHAIN event is written only if it passes all enabled filters: the pid list and the lwp list (an event is skipped when its pid or tid is not in the list, or is in it when exclusive is set), the event list (looks up the event index of the event's pmcid in the map, and calls errx(EX_USAGE, "unallocated pmcid") if the pmcid is not in the map; this check only runs when an event filter was given; then skips by membership as above), and the process-name and thread-name filters (pmc_find_name, inverted by exclusive). The pmcid map, the name lists and the last parse state are not freed. It returns nothing.

name: validate_expr
prose: Recursive grammar check of an expression node chain (static, usr.sbin/pmcstudy/eval_expr.c:63-166). The flags val1_is_set, op_is_set and val2_is_set say what has been seen so far in the current sub-expression, and *op_cnt is the number of currently open parentheses. At the end of the chain (exp == NULL) it returns 0 only if a value-operator-value is complete and no parenthesis is open, otherwise 1. For an operator node: after a complete value-op-value it collapses back to value-op, after a lone value it records the operator, otherwise it prints 'Op but no val1 set' and returns -1. For a value node: it sets val1, or val2 if val1 and an operator are set, otherwise ('val1 set, val2 about to be set op empty') returns -1. For an open parenthesis: if it is the last node it prints a message and calls exit(-1); an operator right after it, a value immediately before it with no operator, or a complete value-op-value before it return -1; otherwise it increments *op_cnt, and with no preceding value it returns the result of validating the rest of the chain starting inside the parenthesis, while with a preceding value-op it validates the inside as a fresh sub-expression (a non-zero result returns -1; zero sets val2 and the walk then continues from the node after the open parenthesis, walking the parenthesised nodes a second time). For a close parenthesis: it decrements *op_cnt and returns 0 if the current sub-expression is a complete value-op-value, else prints 'Found close paren and not complete' and returns -1; nodes after a close parenthesis that returns 0 are not examined by that call. An unknown node type prints a message and calls exit(-5). Since a parenthesised group after an operator is validated as a fresh sub-expression, a single value inside it is incomplete and gives -1. No memory is allocated or freed.
note: usr.sbin/pmcstudy/eval_expr.c:63-166 (end of chain 80-87, operators 89-106, open paren 107-138, close paren 139-148, values 149-158, unknown type 160-162, recursion 165). Reviewer round 1 right (an unclosed paren at the end of the chain returns 1, not -1); round 15 right (a nested group after an operator is walked again and an incomplete inner group returns -1; a close paren returns 0 without looking at later nodes).

name: bundle_StartIdleTimer
prose: Restarts the PPP bundle idle timer (usr.sbin/ppp/bundle.c:1168-1194). It stops bundle->idle.timer first. It then arms the timer only if the open physical-link bits include at least one bit outside PHYS_DEDICATED|PHYS_DDIAL (the test is (open & (DEDICATED|DDIAL)) != open, so open == 0 or open made only of those two bits does not arm it) and bundle->cfg.idle.timeout is non-zero. In that case, with now = time(NULL): if secs is 0 it becomes cfg.idle.timeout; if cfg.idle.min_timeout is greater than secs and bundle->upat is set, it computes up = now - upat and, when min_timeout > up and min_timeout - up exceeds secs, replaces secs with min_timeout - up. It sets the timer function to bundle_IdleTimeout, name "idle", load secs * SECTICKS (using the adjusted secs), arg bundle, starts it with timer_Start, and sets bundle->idle.done = now + the adjusted secs. When the condition is false only the timer stop happens and idle.done is left unchanged. It returns nothing.

name: cbcp_AdjustResponse
prose: Adjusts our CBCP response (cbcp->fsm) to a received REQ (data) so that we agree with the peer (usr.sbin/ppp/cbcp.c:353-471). By request type. CBCP_NONUM: if 'none' is among the configured callback options it sets fsm.type = CBCP_NONUM; in either case it returns 1 (it sends its own desired response when 'none' is not configured). CBCP_CLIENTNUM: only if fsm.type is CBCP_CLIENTNUM: if the peer included an address spec whose type is not PSTN it logs and returns 0; otherwise it truncates fsm.phone at its first ',' (keeping only the first number) and returns 1; if fsm.type is not CBCP_CLIENTNUM it logs 'no number to pass' and returns 0. CBCP_SERVERNUM: if fsm.type is CBCP_SERVERNUM it clears fsm.phone and returns 1; otherwise, if the peer gave an address that is not PSTN it returns 0, and if it is PSTN and fsm.type is CBCP_CLIENTNUM it searches our comma-separated list for the peer's number and on a match sets fsm.type = CBCP_SERVERNUM, copies that number into fsm.phone and returns 1; if nothing matched it logs 'Peer won't allow local decision' and returns 0. CBCP_LISTNUM: only if fsm.type is CBCP_CLIENTNUM or CBCP_LISTNUM, it walks the peer's addresses (logging unrecognised types) and, for the first PSTN number that is in our list, sets fsm.type = CBCP_LISTNUM, copies the number to fsm.phone and returns 1; otherwise it logs 'no good number' and returns 0. Any other REQ type logs 'Unrecognised REQ type' and returns 0. The fsm is changed only on the paths that return 1 (and NONUM may leave it unchanged while returning 1).
note: usr.sbin/ppp/cbcp.c:353-471 (NONUM 362-377, CLIENTNUM 379-402, SERVERNUM 404-440, LISTNUM 441-466, unknown 469-470). Reviewer rounds 1 and 15 right: CBCP_NONUM returns 1 even when 'none' is not configured, without changing fsm.type.

name: CcpSendConfigReq
prose: Builds and sends a CCP Configure-Request (usr.sbin/ppp/ccp.c:344-396). It resets ccp->my_proto and ccp->out.algorithm to -1 and sets alloc = (his_reject == 0 && out.opt == NULL). For each algorithm f in table order that is enabled in the configuration, not rejected by the peer and for which Usable(fp) returns true: when alloc is false it searches ccp->out.opt for an existing node with the same id and algorithm index; if a node was found it is reused, else (no match, or alloc true) a new ccp_opt is malloc'ed and linked at the tail (header length 2, algorithm index f, filled by the algorithm's OptInit); a malloc failure logs 'Not enough memory' and stops the loop. If the option does not fit in the remaining part of the 100-byte buffer it logs 'CCP REQ buffer overrun' and stops the loop (a node created for that algorithm stays on the out.opt list although it was not copied into the packet). Otherwise it copies the option bytes into the buffer, sets ccp->my_proto to its id and ccp->out.algorithm to f (so they record the last option appended, or stay -1 if none), and, when alloc is true, advances the list tail pointer. After the loop, whether it ended normally or early, it always calls fsm_Output(fp, CODE_CONFIGREQ, fp->reqid, buff, length) with the options collected so far (possibly none). No memory is freed here. It returns nothing.
note: usr.sbin/ppp/ccp.c:344-396 (alloc 355, loop 358-393, reuse search 363-366, malloc 368-373, overrun 381-384, output 395). Reviewer round 1 right (a partial packet is sent on malloc or buffer failure); round 15 right (when alloc is false any matching node is reused and unmatched algorithms still get new nodes, not only when his_reject is non-zero).

name: SetVariable
prose: Implements the ppp 'set <variable>' commands (static, usr.sbin/ppp/command.c:1652-2357). It picks the variable from arg->cmd->args and the first argument (or the empty string), chooses a link, and first checks context: a command that requires a link context (LOCAL_CX) without one logs a warning and returns 1; a context given to a command that does not use one is ignored. A large switch then applies the variable and sets res (initially 0), which is returned at the end (line 2356). Outcomes seen in the part read: authkey and authname are copied with truncation (authname with a warning if not in DEAD/ESTABLISH phase); autoload needs exactly three arguments (otherwise res = 1) and an invalid minimum, maximum (smaller than the minimum) or period gives res = 1; window size: an invalid outgoing or incoming value is only logged and replaced by 15 (res stays 0), and a missing argument gives res = 1; MPPE returns -1 (res = -1) for too many arguments, a bits value other than 40, 56 or 128 or an invalid state; mode is -1 for PHYS_NONE/PHYS_ALL; MRRU, MRU and MTU return 1 for values that are too small or too large (or the wrong phase for MRRU) and -1 for a non-numeric argument or a bad keyword; DNS/NBNS addresses that do not parse make the function return -1 directly (lines 2135 and 2139); the SetRetry-based variables (retry periods) return SetRetry's result; other variables return 1 for missing or invalid arguments (several checks between lines 1997 and 2357) and 0 otherwise. On an error return processing stops, with possibly some already-parsed values stored. Only lines 1652-1998 and the return statements of the rest were read; the remaining variable cases (openmode, idle timeout, RADIUS, parity, speed and others) were not read in detail.

name: NegotiateSet
prose: Implements the ppp 'enable/disable/accept/deny <option>' commands for the negotiation options (static, usr.sbin/ppp/command.c:2849-2976; the slice 2941-3191 starts near its end). It calls ident_cmd(arg->argv[arg->argn - 2], &keep, &add) and returns 1 if the keyword is not recognised. If the command table requires a link context (LOCAL_CX) and arg->cx is NULL it logs a warning and returns 2; a context given to a command that does not use one is ignored (cx set to NULL). It then switches on the NEG_* option in arg->cmd->args. For the CHAP/PAP/ACFCOMP/PROTOCOMP/LQR options it updates the corresponding field in cx->physical->link.lcp.cfg, for MPPE/DEFLATE/PPPDDEFLATE/PRED1 the l->ccp.cfg.neg entry, for DNS, ENDDISC and VJCOMP the bundle's ipcp/mp configuration, each as (field & keep) | add. Options that use cx->physical dereference cx, which is non-NULL only for commands flagged LOCAL_CX (checked before the switch). It returns 0 after a successful update.

name: datalink_HangupDone
prose: Called when the physical link has hung up (usr.sbin/ppp/datalink.c:115-186). If the physical type is PHYS_DEDICATED, the bundle is not cleaning up and the descriptor is not -1, it keeps the device open, calls datalink_LoginDone(dl) and returns (LoginDone can change the state or call back into this function). Otherwise it calls chat_Finish, physical_Close and sets phone.chosen to "N/A", and then takes one of three branches. (1) If a callback is required (cbcp.required): it logs the callback number, clears the callback option mask, copies the callback phone into cfg.phone.list, resets phone.alt/next, sets reconnect_tries and dial.tries to their configured maxima and dial.incs to 0, requests a script run in packet mode, sets the mode to PHYS_BACKGROUND (logging an error if that fails), calls bundle_LinksRemoved, raises cbcp.fsm.delay to the dial timeout if smaller, starts the dial timer with that delay, calls cbcp_Down, moves to DATALINK_OPENING and, if the bundle phase is DEAD or TERMINATE, to PHASE_ESTABLISH. (2) Else if the bundle is cleaning up, the type is PHYS_DIRECT, or there are no dial tries left (dial.tries == 0, or negative with no reconnect tries) for a type that is neither DDIAL nor DEDICATED: it moves to DATALINK_CLOSED, sets dial.tries to -1, dial.incs to 0 and reconnect_tries to 0, calls bundle_LinkClosed, and starts a dial timer (datalink_GetDialTimeout) unless the bundle is cleaning up or the type is DIRECT, BACKGROUND or FOREGROUND. (3) Otherwise it moves to DATALINK_OPENING (and PHASE_ESTABLISH if the phase was DEAD or TERMINATE): if dial.tries < 0 it starts the reconnect timer, resets dial.tries to the maximum and dial.incs to 0, decrements reconnect_tries, logs and notifies EX_RECONNECT; else it starts the dial timer (the dial timeout, or the next-number timeout when another number follows) and notifies EX_REDIAL, without resetting any counters. It returns nothing.
note: usr.sbin/ppp/datalink.c:115-186 (dedicated 117-122, callback 128-151, closed 152-163, reconnect/redial 164-185). Reviewer round 1 right (the function itself calls chat_Finish and physical_Close, and the dedicated path can go on through LoginDone); round 15 right (the redial branch at 178-183 does not reset the counters; only the reconnect branch does).

name: datalink_Up
prose: Starts or advances opening of a datalink (usr.sbin/ppp/datalink.c:963-1000). If OPT_FORCE_SCRIPTS is not enabled and the physical type includes PHYS_DIRECT or PHYS_DEDICATED, runscripts is forced to 0. It then switches on dl->state. DATALINK_CLOSED: if the bundle phase is PHASE_DEAD or PHASE_TERMINATE it moves the bundle to PHASE_ESTABLISH; it moves dl to DATALINK_OPENING, sets reconnect_tries to 0 for PHYS_DIRECT and cfg.reconnect.max otherwise, sets dial.tries to cfg.dial.max, and sets script.run = runscripts and script.packetmode = packetmode. DATALINK_OPENING: if script.run is 0 and runscripts is non-zero it sets script.run = 1 (this is the only state where script.run is raised), then falls through. DATALINK_OPENING, DATALINK_DIAL, DATALINK_LOGIN and DATALINK_READY: if script.packetmode is 0 and packetmode is non-zero it sets script.packetmode = 1, and in DATALINK_READY only it also clears script.run to 0 and moves to DATALINK_CARRIER. Any other state changes nothing. It returns nothing.

name: exec_Create
prose: Real name exec_Create (usr.sbin/ppp/exec.c:241-410; the slice 302-410 is its tail). It starts with dev = NULL. If p->fd < 0 and the device name starts with '!': it mallocs an exec device (a failure logs and returns NULL), decrements p->fd, and creates a stream or datagram socketpair (on failure it logs, frees dev and sets it to NULL), sets fids[0] non-blocking, creates a pidpipe (on failure it closes the socketpair, frees dev and sets it to NULL) and forks. If fork fails it logs and closes the four descriptors but does not free dev, so a device is still returned with p->fd negative. In the child it closes its unused ends, terminates the timer service, drops privileges, vfork()s a grandchild that parses the command line (MakeArgs failure: _exit(ESRCH)), expands it, dups fids[1] onto stdin, stdout and stderr, marks other descriptors close-on-exec and execvp's the command (on failure it prints a message and _exit's with errno); the intermediate child writes the grandchild's pid to the pidpipe and exits. In the parent it closes fids[1], reads the pid into p->session_owner (set to -1 if the read is short), waits for the child (retrying on EINTR); a waitpid error, a child killed by a signal or a non-zero exit status close fids[0], set p->session_owner to -1 and leave p->fd negative, while success or a stopped child sets p->fd = fids[0]. If p->fd >= 0 on entry and fstat shows a FIFO, it mallocs a device (failure only logs, leaving dev NULL); when p->fd is stdin it sets fd_out = dup(STDOUT_FILENO) and installs exec_UpdateSet and exec_IsSet on p->desc, otherwise fd_out = -1. Finally, if dev is non-NULL it copies baseexecdevice into dev->dev, calls physical_SetupStack, logs a warning if the carrier setting is not CD_DEFAULT and returns &dev->dev (the caller owns the allocation); otherwise it returns NULL.

name: fsm_Down
prose: Handles the lower layer going down for a PPP FSM (usr.sbin/ppp/fsm.c:313-343). It switches on fp->state with no default case. ST_CLOSED: NewState to ST_INITIAL. ST_CLOSING: calls fp->fn->LayerFinish(fp), moves to ST_INITIAL, then calls the parent's LayerFinish. ST_STOPPED: moves to ST_STARTING, then calls fp->fn->LayerStart(fp) and the parent's LayerStart. ST_STOPPING, ST_REQSENT, ST_ACKRCVD and ST_ACKSENT: only NewState to ST_STARTING. ST_OPENED: calls fp->fn->LayerDown(fp), moves to ST_STARTING, then calls the parent's LayerDown. ST_INITIAL and ST_STARTING (and any other value) are not handled: nothing happens, no message is logged and the state is unchanged (the 'Oops, Up' message belongs to fsm_Up's default case, not here). It returns nothing.
note: usr.sbin/ppp/fsm.c:313-343 (cases 317-341, no default); fsm_Up default log at 306-309. Reviewer round 1 right (CLOSING goes to INITIAL and STOPPED to STARTING); round 15 wrong in detail (ST_INITIAL is not handled at all; it neither logs nor moves to ST_CLOSED) but right that the old 'Oops, Up' claim was wrong.

name: FsmRecvConfigRej
prose: Handles a received Config-Reject (RCJ) packet (usr.sbin/ppp/fsm.c:802-867). It computes the payload length plen = m_length(bp) and flen = header length - sizeof header; if the payload is shorter than flen it frees bp and returns without sending anything. Otherwise it calls lcp_SendIdentification on the link's LCP and switches on the state: ST_INITIAL and ST_STARTING log 'Oops, RCJ' and free bp and return; ST_CLOSED and ST_STOPPED call SendTerminateAck with the packet id, free bp and return; ST_CLOSING and ST_STOPPING free bp and return. In the remaining states it pulls up the mbuf, decodes the rejected options with fp->fn->DecodeConfig in MODE_REJ (logging '[EMPTY]' if there are none), and then: ST_REQSENT and ST_ACKSENT restart the request timer and send a new Config-Req (state unchanged); ST_OPENED calls LayerDown, sends a Config-Req, moves to ST_REQSENT and calls the parent's LayerDown; ST_ACKRCVD sends a Config-Req and moves to ST_REQSENT. Finally it frees bp, so bp is freed on every path, but the Identification is sent only when the payload length check passed. It returns nothing.
note: usr.sbin/ppp/fsm.c:802-867 (length check 810-815, identification 817, early states 822-838, decode 840-847, state actions 849-865, free 866). Reviewer round 1 right (INITIAL/STARTING/CLOSED/STOPPED/CLOSING/STOPPING return early with no state update); round 15 right (the short-payload path returns before lcp_SendIdentification).

name: FilterCheck
prose: Real name FilterCheck (usr.sbin/ppp/ip.c:209-493; the packet name was truncated). It returns 0 to permit and 1 to deny a packet against a ppp filter, and sets *psecs to the matching permit rule's timeout when psecs is non-NULL. If the first rule's action is A_NONE (an empty filter) it returns 0 immediately. It reads the addresses, length and protocol from the IPv6 header (family AF_INET6) or the IPv4 header; for IPv4, if the fragment offset is non-zero it logs and returns 1 for an offset below 3 units (a fragment that could overwrite the header), else returns 1 if the filter does not allow fragments (fragok clear) and 0 if it does. It then walks the rules from index 0 while n < MAXFILTERS: a rule with action A_NONE is skipped (n++); otherwise the source and destination ranges (unspecified ranges match anything) and, when the rule names a protocol, the protocol-specific fields are compared; before ports are examined the payload is checked for its minimum size (ICMP/ICMPv6/IGMP/OSPF 8 bytes, GRE 2, IPv6 20, UDP 8, TCP at least 20 octets and at least its declared header length) and a short datagram logs and returns 1. When (match != the rule's invert flag): a rule whose action is below A_NONE is a jump (n and the rule pointer are set to that rule index and the walk continues); A_PERMIT sets *psecs, logs for the DIAL filter, and returns 0; any other action logs the deny and returns 1. A non-matching rule advances to the next one. If no rule decides, it logs 'implicit deny' and returns 1. It does not modify the packet or the filter.

name: LcpDecodeConfig
prose: Real name LcpDecodeConfig (usr.sbin/ppp/lcp.c:659-1297; the slice 1030-1297 is its tail). It decodes the LCP option bytes cp..end for the given mode (MODE_REQ, MODE_NAK, MODE_REJ, MODE_NOP) into the decode context dec, returning nothing. It loops while at least an option header remains, reading each option with fsm_readopt (a NULL result ends the loop), logging it, and handling it by option id (MRRU, MRU, ACCMAP, AUTHPROTO, QUALPROTO, MAGICNUM, PROTOCOMP, ACFCOMP, CALLBACK, SHORTSEQ, ENDDISC and others). In MODE_REQ each option is acknowledged (fsm_ack), negotiated down or up with a Nak (fsm_nak, for instance MRRU is clamped to MAX_MRU/MIN_MRU) or rejected (fsm_rej, which also sets the my_reject bit for that option); an unknown option is logged and, in MODE_REQ, rejected with my_reject set. In MODE_NAK the lcp want_* values are adjusted, and in MODE_REJ the his_reject bit is set for the option (and the want_* value cleared) in most cases; callbacks are special: a Nak of a callback removes our most preferred callback method from want_callback.opmask without setting his_reject and calls fsm_Close if none is left, and a Reject of callback sets his_reject (and clears the mask) only if 'none' was an acceptable callback, else logs 'Peer rejected *required* callback' and calls fsm_Close. A matching magic number in a REQ makes it generate a new magic number, Nak it, arm ualarm and call sigsuspend. After the loop, unless the mode is MODE_NOP: for a REQ on a PHYS_DIRECT link that requires callback (opmask set without 'none') and did not contain a callback option it appends a callback Nak; for a REQ when no MRU was requested (mru_req not set) and the default MRU limited by the device MTU and max MTU is below DEF_MRU it sets his_mru, appends an MRU Nak and sets mru_req; finally it calls fsm_opt_normalise(dec). Only the head, the MRRU case, the callback and magic cases and the tail were read in detail; the other option cases (lines 727-1236) were only checked for their reject, close and ack/nak calls.

name: ng_Create
prose: Real name ng_Create (usr.sbin/ppp/netgraph.c:453-743; the slice 508-743 is its tail). Creates a netgraph device for physical link p and returns &dev->dev, or NULL. Path 1 (p->fd < 0 and the device name starts with the netgraph prefix): it decrements p->fd, mallocs the device (NULL on failure, without freeing anything else), loads the netgraph modules, and creates a socket node with ID0NgMkSockNode (on failure it logs, frees dev, sets p->fd = -2 and returns NULL). It then parses the path after the prefix, word by word, using getsegment: it builds or checks nodes and hooks, sending NGM_LISTHOOKS requests (a send or receive failure aborts), reusing an existing hook if it is already connected to the expected peer hook and node type (a different one aborts), creating peers with NGM_MKPEER and naming nodes with NgNameNode; syntax errors (a missing hook segment, a second hook at the end, a missing '[' before a node, an empty [nodetype:nodename], no initial node name, or no node type after the first node) abort too. 'Abort' means ng_Abandon(dev, p): it closes dev->cs and p->fd, sets p->fd = -2, frees dev and returns NULL. After the walk it records the final hook in dev->hook, connects the socket node to it with NGM_CONNECT (failure: ng_Abandon), installs ng_UpdateSet, ng_IsSet and ng_DescriptorRead on p->desc and copies basengdevice into the device. Path 2 (otherwise): if getsockname on p->fd says it is an AF_NETGRAPH socket it mallocs a device (failure logs and returns NULL), copies basengdevice, sets dev->cs = -1 and an empty hook, and installs no descriptor handlers and sends no NGM_CONNECT. If dev is non-NULL at the end it calls physical_SetupStack(p, dev->dev.name, PHYSICAL_FORCE_SYNCNOACF) and returns &dev->dev; otherwise it returns NULL without Abandon (neither path applied). The caller owns the returned device.

name: prompt_Read
prose: Reads input on a ppp prompt descriptor (usr.sbin/ppp/prompt.c:183-301; the fdset argument is unused and nothing is returned). In command mode (p->TermMode == NULL) it reads up to LINE_LEN - 1 bytes from fd_in. If n > 0 it strips one trailing newline, sets nonewline, calls prompt_Required, and, only if the line is non-empty, decodes it with command_Decode (printing 'Syntax error' if that fails) with log_PromptContext temporarily set to the prompt when it was NULL (it is then reset to its previous value). If n <= 0 (end of file or error) it logs 'Client connection closed', calls Cleanup() when the prompt has no owner, and calls prompt_Destroy. In terminal mode it switches on the datalink state: DATALINK_CLOSED prints 'Link lost, terminal mode', returns to command mode and requests a prompt; DATALINK_OPEN prints 'Packet mode detected', returns to command mode and returns; any other state except DATALINK_READY returns without reading. In DATALINK_READY it reads one byte; for n > 0 and readtilde == 0 a '~' sets readtilde = 1 (and is not forwarded), any other byte is written to the physical link (a failed write logs and switches to command mode); with readtilde == 1 the next byte is an escape: '?' help, 'p' packet mode (datalink_Up(..., 0, 1) and command mode), '.' command mode with a prompt request, 't' show timers, 'm' show mbufs, any other byte is forwarded to the physical link as in the first case; readtilde is then cleared. A read of 0 or -1 in terminal mode does nothing.

name: radius_Process
prose: Handles the result of a RADIUS request (usr.sbin/ppp/radius.c:258-659; returns nothing). It sets r->cx.fd = -1 (stop select()ing) and chooses 'auth' or 'acct' from whether r->cx.auth is set. It then switches on got and, on every path, ends by calling rad_close(r->cx.rad). RAD_ACCESS_ACCEPT and RAD_ACCESS_REJECT without an auth state: log, close and return with no parsing and no auth callback. RAD_ACCESS_CHALLENGE, an unexpected RAD_ACCOUNTING_RESPONSE, -1 and any other code: log, call auth_Failure if r->cx.auth is set, close and return. For ACCEPT or REJECT with an auth state it first resets ip and mask to INADDR_NONE, mtu and vj to 0, then loops over the reply attributes with rad_get_attr: framed IP address, netmask, MTU, compression, routing, session timeout, filter id, reply message, IPv6 prefix, Microsoft vendor attributes (CHAP error, CHAP2 success, MPPE policy, types and keys) store into r (replacing the previous string or key, which are freed first), while framed IPv4 and IPv6 routes are parsed and added with route_Add to the existing route lists (not replacing them); a malformed string, vendor attribute or route value that fails its check calls auth_Failure, rad_close and returns early. After the loop: if rad_get_attr returned -1 it logs and calls auth_Failure; else if got is RAD_ACCESS_REJECT it calls auth_Failure; else it sets r->valid = 1 and calls auth_Success. It then calls rad_close.

Reviewer round 1 right (malformed attributes can call auth_Failure and return early); round 15 right (routes are accumulated with route_Add at 447 and 525, not replaced). name: radius_Authenticate
prose: Sends a RADIUS access request for the given authentication data (usr.sbin/ppp/radius.c:903-1080; returns 1 when a request is or will be pending, 0 when it was not sent). It returns 0 immediately if r->cfg.file is empty, and returns 1 without changing anything if r->cx.fd is already set (a request is in flight; it assumes the same credentials). Otherwise it calls radius_Destroy(r), opens a RADIUS handle with rad_auth_open (NULL: log and return 0), loads the config file (rad_config failure: close and return 0), creates an ACCESS_REQUEST (failure: close, return 0) and puts User-Name, Service-Type Framed and Framed-Protocol PPP (failure: close, return 0). By the negotiated protocol it adds the PAP password attribute, or for CHAP type 0x5 the CHAP password and challenge attributes (either failing: close, return 0), or for CHAP 0x80 (MSCHAP, key length must be 50) and 0x81 (MSCHAPv2, key length must be sizeof(struct MSCHAPv2_resp) + 1) the Microsoft vendor challenge and response attributes; a wrong key length or an unrecognised CHAP type logs, closes and returns 0, but the return values of the rad_put_vendor_attr calls for MSCHAP/MSCHAPv2 are not checked, so a failure there does not stop the request. It then adds NAS-IP-Address or NAS-Identifier (a failed put: close, return 0; a gethostname failure only logs) and the Calling-Station-Id/physical details (failure: close, return 0), logs, sets r->cx.auth = authp and calls rad_init_send_request: if that returns non-zero it calls radius_Process(r, got) immediately, else it logs 'Request sent' and starts r->cx.timer with radius_Timeout. It then returns 1.

name: sl_uncompress_tcp
prose: Van Jacobson TCP/IP header decompression for one received packet (usr.sbin/ppp/slcompress.c:428-584). *bufp points at the packet, len is its length. For TYPE_UNCOMPRESSED_TCP it treats the IP header's protocol field as the connection index: an index above max_state goes to bad; otherwise it sets comp->last_recv to it and clears SLF_TOSS, restores ip_p to IPPROTO_TCP, computes the header length from the IP and TCP header-length fields (a header that does not fit in len, or longer than MAX_HDR, goes to bad, after SLF_TOSS was already cleared), copies the header into comp->rstate[index], sets cs_hlen, increments sls_uncompressedin and returns len unchanged. Any other type except TYPE_COMPRESSED_TCP goes to bad. For TYPE_COMPRESSED_TCP it increments sls_compressedin and decodes the change byte: with NEW_C the next byte is the new state index (greater than max_state, or last_recv still 255, goes to bad; otherwise SLF_TOSS is cleared and last_recv set); without NEW_C, if SLF_TOSS is set it increments sls_tossed and returns 0 (not an error and not a change to SLF_TOSS). It then updates the saved header in comp->rstate[last_recv] from the compressed fields (checksum, push flag, the special deltas or the explicit urgent/window/ack/seq changes, and the IP id), without checking that the compressed bytes read lie inside len; len is reduced by the bytes consumed and a negative result goes to bad; otherwise it sets *bufp to just before the data so the rebuilt header precedes it, sets the IP total length, recomputes the IP header checksum, copies the header into the buffer and returns the new length. 'bad' sets SLF_TOSS, increments sls_errorin and returns 0. The packet buffer must have room before *bufp for the rebuilt header.

name: tty_Create
prose: Real name tty_Create (usr.sbin/ppp/tty.c:675-770; the slice 757-770 is its tail, and the packet called it tty_Open). It returns NULL, without touching the descriptor, if p->fd is negative or not a tty (isatty). It mallocs a ttydevice; on failure it closes p->fd, sets p->fd = -1 and returns NULL. It copies in basettydevice, initialises the timer and modem bits, reads the current termios with tcgetattr (the result is not checked) and saves it in dev->ios, applies a configured carrier override, then puts the line in raw mode (cfmakeraw) with CLOCAL, hardware or software flow control, IXON, HUPCL unless the link is dedicated and, unless the link is PHYS_DIRECT, the configured parity and speed (a cfsetspeed failure is only logged). name: read_userconfig
prose: Reads the pw configuration file file into the static config structure and returns &config (usr.sbin/pw/pw_conf.c:241-407; the slice is its middle and tail). If fopen(file, "r") fails it returns &config immediately with nothing changed. Otherwise it reads lines with getline; for each line whose first token (delimiters space, tab, CR, LF, '=') does not start with '#', it takes the next token q and matches the keyword against kwds[]. Handlers: default password (passwd_val), reuse_uids, reuse_gids (boolean_val); nispasswd, dotdir, newmail, logfile, default_class: NULL when q is missing or not a true boolean, else a newstr copy; home root: the literal "/home" in the default case, else a copy; shell directory: the literal "/bin" or a copy; default shell: bourne_shell or a copy; home mode: _DEF_DIRMODE by default, else the result of setmode/getmode (an invalid mode string calls errx(1, "Invalid mode: '%s'", q)); the shells list: up to _UC_MAXSHELLS tokens copied into system_shells, and the remaining entries set to NULL when at least one was given; default group: NULL unless the name is valid and getgrnam finds it, else a copy; extra groups: each remaining token is appended to config.groups (created on first use); min/max uid and gid and expire/password days are parsed with strtounum/strtonum, but the value is assigned to the config field before errstr is tested, so an invalid number gives a warnx 'ignoring' message while the field has already been set to the function's error return (0). Unknown keywords are ignored. At the end it frees the getline buffer, closes the file and returns &config. Strings taken from the file are newly allocated and owned by config, but the defaults ("/home", "/bin", bourne_shell) are static literals.

name: pw_group_add
prose: Implements 'pw groupadd' (usr.sbin/pw/pw_group.c:502-587; slice cut the head). If arg1 is non-NULL it is taken as a numeric group id (all digits, through pw_checkid with GID_MAX) or as the group name. getopt then handles -C config file, -q, -n name, -g gid (pw_checkid), -H fd (precrypted; errx(EX_USAGE) if -h or -H was already given, or if pw_checkfd returns '-'), -h fd (errx(EX_USAGE) if -H or -h was already given), -M members, -o (sets conf.checkduplicate = false), -N (dry run), -P (pretty) and -Y (NIS); an unknown option or any leftover operand calls usage() (EX_USAGE). name: pw_user_add
prose: Implements 'pw useradd' (usr.sbin/pw/pw_user.c:1194-1526; the slice 1327-1627 covers its tail and the start of the next function). It parses arg1 (a numeric uid via pw_checkid or a login name) and the options (-C, -q, -n, -u, -c, -d, -e, -p, -g, -G, -m, -M, -k (errx(EX_OSFILE) if the skeleton directory is missing or not a directory), -s, -o, -L, -i, -w, -H/-h (errx(EX_USAGE) if both were given or -H gets '-'), -D, -b, -N, -P, -y, -Y); an unknown option or leftover operand calls usage(). Unless -N it requires root (pw_check_root), with -q it reopens stderr onto /dev/null, and loads the configuration. With -D it errx(EX_DATAERR)s if -n was also given, applies the min/max uid/gid values, writes the configuration file and returns EXIT_SUCCESS (err(EX_IOERR, "config update") if the write fails). Otherwise it needs a user id or name (errx(EX_DATAERR) 'user name or id required' or 'login name required') and errx(EX_DATAERR) if the login already exists; it builds the passwd entry, sets a password from the -h/-H descriptor if given. Otherwise it adds the passwd entry with addpwent (-1: errx(EX_IOERR) 'already exists'; any other failure: err(EX_IOERR, "passwd file update")); with -Y and a -y path starting with '/' it also adds an NIS passwd entry, where failures are only warnings. It adds the user to the supplementary groups from -G (groups that cannot be found or updated are skipped), errx(EX_NOUSER) if the new passwd entry cannot be found again, logs the addition, touches and chowns the mail file unless an alternate directory is used, creates and populates the home directory when -m was given (and no alternate directory), sends the welcome mail through sendmail when a newmail file is configured, and, only if -Y was given and nis_update() returned 0, logs 'NIS maps updated' (a failing nis_update is silently ignored). It returns EXIT_SUCCESS in the normal case, print_user's result for -N, and does not return after the errx/err exits.

name: rm_r
prose: Removes the directory tree path (relative to the directory descriptor rootfd; a leading '/' is skipped for the *at calls but the original string is kept for dataset removal) and returns true if anything remains or could not be removed (usr.sbin/pw/rm_r.c:58-111). openat(O_DIRECTORY) failing or fdopendir failing (the descriptor is then closed) returns true. For each entry other than '.' and '..': an fstatat failure skips the entry silently (not counted); a directory is processed recursively and a true result sets skipped; a symlink is unlinked regardless of its owner, and a non-directory owned by uid is unlinked, while a non-directory owned by someone else sets skipped (unlinkat failures on these entries are ignored and not counted). After closedir it calls fstatat on path: if that fails it returns the current skipped value (false when nothing was skipped). If path is a symlink it unlinks it (failure sets skipped); else if it is owned by uid it removes the directory with unlinkat(AT_REMOVEDIR), and on failure, if errno is EBUSY and nothing was skipped so far, skipped becomes the result of try_dataset_remove(original path) (which returns true unless the ZFS dataset was destroyed), else skipped becomes true; if it is owned by someone else skipped becomes true. It returns skipped. The DIR stream (and its descriptor) is closed on every path after fdopendir succeeds.

name: client_request
prose: Starts the lock-request client process of rpc.lockd (usr.sbin/rpc.lockd/kern.c:122-230; it returns the child's pid in the parent and does not return in the child). It opens the NFS lock device O_RDWR|O_NONBLOCK; if that fails it logs and goes to the err label, which restores euid 0 and calls _exit(1), so the calling process itself exits (before any fork). It ignores SIGPIPE and forks: a fork failure calls err(1, "fork") (the euid is not restored there); in the parent it sets the title 'server' and returns the child pid, leaving devfd open. In the child it sets the title 'client', installs client_cleanup for SIGHUP and SIGTERM (which restores euid 0 and calls exit(-1), i.e. status 255), records the owner time and pid and the host name, looks up the daemon user (getpwnam failure: log and err label, _exit(1)) and sets the effective uid to it. It then loops forever: it reads a fixed-size LOCKD_MSG from the device; a full message is logged if tracing is on, an lm_version other than LOCKD_MSG_VERSION is only logged (the message is still dispatched), and it is handled by lock type: F_RDLCK and F_WRLCK call test_request when lm_getlk is set and lock_request otherwise, F_UNLCK calls unlock_request, and any other type is logged and counted as a failure (ret = 1). A non-zero ret makes it write a lockd_ans with la_errno EHOSTUNREACH to the device with nfslockdans (a failure of that write is logged). A read error other than EAGAIN logs and goes to the err label (euid 0, _exit(1)); a short non-empty read is logged as discarded bytes; a zero-length read or EAGAIN just continues.

Reviewer round 1 right (open failure exits before the fork); round 2 right (unknown lm_version is only logged); round 15 right (fork failure uses err(1) without restoring euid). test_request, lock_request, unlock_request and nfslockdans were not read.

name: main
prose: Entry point of rpc.statd (usr.sbin/rpc.statd/statd.c:80-315; slice cut the head). It parses -d (debug), -F (foreground), -h host (a copied host list) and -p port (an invalid port or an unknown option calls usage()), then unregisters the SM program with rpcb_unset and checks whether an IPv6 socket can be created (have_v6 = 0 if not). It builds the host list: '*' when no -h was given, otherwise the given hosts plus ::1 (only when have_v6) and 127.0.0.1 (allocation failures free the list and exit(1)). It walks the netconfig entries and for every NC_VISIBLE transport except inet6 when have_v6 is 0 calls create_service, retrying with a new dynamic port up to GETPORT_MAXTRY times on EADDRINUSE and exit(1)ing on persistent bind failure, out of memory, or more port numbers than the port_list can hold. It then walks the netconfig again and calls complete_service for each of those same visible transports (again skipping inet6 when have_v6 is 0), using a port from port_list or svcport_str, and frees sock_fd and the port_list entries. It calls init_file("/var/db/statd.status"), daemonizes unless -F was given (err(1, "cannot fork") if daemon fails), opens the syslog, installs the SIGCHLD handler, calls notify_hosts (which may fork) and svc_run. svc_run should not return; if it does main calls exit(1). Main does not return normally.

name: yppasswdproc_update_master_1_svc
prose: Real name yppasswdproc_update_master_1_svc (usr.sbin/rpc.yppasswdd/yppasswdd_server.c:745-954; the slice 777-954 is its middle and tail). RPC handler that updates a user's master.passwd entry. It returns a pointer to a static int, initialised to 1, which is changed to 0 only at the very end on success (line 952). It first rejects (svcerr_auth AUTH_BADCRED and return with result 1) a caller whose socket family is not AF_UNIX, whose credential flavor is not AUTH_SYS, whose local uid cannot be obtained or is not 0. It looks up the user in the domain's master.passwd.byname map: if that fails and additions are not allowed (-a) it logs and returns result 1; a successful lookup copies the existing record. validate_master failing (bad arguments) returns result 1. For a domain other than the default it uses <yp_dir>/<domain>/master.passwd. It then runs pw_init, pw_lock, pw_tmp and pw_copy (each failure calls pw_fini where relevant, logs and returns result 1 with nothing renamed), renames the current file to <file>.hold (failure: pw_fini, log, return 1) and then either runs pw_mkdb for the system master.passwd (failure: log and restore the .hold copy) or renames the temporary file into place (failure: log and restore the .hold copy), returning result 1 in those failure cases. After pw_fini, with in-place updates it calls update_inplace (a failure only logs). It forks: in the child it execs the map update program (if exec fails it logs, unlinks the file, restores the .hold copy and exit(1)); if fork fails it logs, unlinks the file, restores the .hold copy and returns result 1; in the parent it unlinks the .hold file. It logs the update, sets result = 0 and returns it. A later exec failure in the child does not change the parent's result, which is 0.

name: rm_ifinfo_index
prose: Removes the interface information for interface index idx (usr.sbin/rtadvd/config.c:194-207). It looks the entry up with if_indextoifinfo(idx); if there is none it logs an error and returns -1. Otherwise it returns rm_ifinfo(ifi) (config.c:209-285). rm_ifinfo returns 0 at once if the entry is already IFI_STATE_UNCONFIGURED. Otherwise it marks it UNCONFIGURED, removes its RA timer (and sets ifi_ra_timer to NULL), then removes the entry from ifilist if it is not persistent, or recreates an empty entry with update_persist_ifinfo if it is persistent. The following switch that is meant to release the RA information (rm_rainfo) tests the state again, which is now UNCONFIGURED, so neither its CONFIGURED nor its TRANSITIVE case can match: rm_rainfo is not called, its error returns are unreachable and the rainfo is not freed here. Finally a non-persistent ifinfo is freed with free(ifi) and rm_ifinfo returns 0. So rm_ifinfo_index returns -1 only when no entry exists for idx and 0 otherwise; a persistent entry stays in the list. The caller must not use a non-persistent ifinfo afterwards.

Reviewer round 1 right (a persistent or already-unconfigured entry is not removed from the list); round 15 right (the rm_rainfo branches are unreachable because ifi_state has just been set to UNCONFIGURED).

name: cm_handler_client
prose: Client side of the rtadvd control protocol (usr.sbin/rtadvd/control_client.c:58-133). buf_orig must be a readable and writable message buffer whose header has cm_type and cm_len (and which is large enough for a reply). It zeroes a local CM_MSG_MAXLEN buffer; if cm_orig->cm_len > CM_MSG_MAXLEN it closes fd and returns -1. It copies cm_type into the local header and, when cm_len is larger than the header, copies the payload and cm_len too (otherwise the local cm_len stays 0). It then runs a state loop until CM_STATE_EOM: CM_STATE_INIT just moves to EOM; CM_STATE_MSG_DISPATCH sets the version and sends the local message with cm_send (on failure it logs and returns -1 without closing fd), then waits for the acknowledgement; CM_STATE_ACK_WAIT receives a reply with cm_recv (failure: close fd and return -1), and a reply of type CM_TYPE_ACK is accepted, while CM_TYPE_ERR or any other type closes fd and returns -1; on ACK it copies the reply into buf_orig with memcpy of the reply's own cm_len bytes (that length is not checked against the buffer here) and moves to EOM. After the loop it closes fd and returns 0. So buf_orig is overwritten only on the ACK path; for states INIT and EOM it is left unchanged.

Reviewer round 1 right (INIT/EOM return 0 without copying a reply into buf_orig); round 15 right (buf_orig must also be writable and big enough for the reply, and its header is read).

name: rtadvd_check_timer
prose: Runs the expired timers of rtadvd and returns the next select() timeout (usr.sbin/rtadvd/timer.c:166-195). It reads CLOCK_MONOTONIC_FAST into now and sets tm_max = tm_limit (the global limit set up by the timer module). For each timer on ra_timer whose rat_tm is at or before now it calls the expire callback with its data; if that returns NULL the timer is treated as removed and the loop continues with the next one without any further handling of that timer (no update call, no tm_max update). Otherwise, if rat_update is non-NULL it calls it with rat_update_data and a pointer to rat_tm, which is expected to store the new interval in rat_tm; then it sets rat_tm = now + rat_tm. When rat_update is NULL, rat_tm is the old absolute deadline, so the new value is now plus that old absolute time rather than now plus an interval. After handling, each timer's rat_tm that is earlier than tm_max becomes the new tm_max. At the end, if tm_max still equals tm_limit it returns NULL; if tm_max is already before now it returns a pointer to the static timespec set to zero; otherwise it returns a pointer to that static timespec holding tm_max - now, valid only until the next call. The expire callback may remove timers while the list is being iterated.
note: usr.sbin/rtadvd/timer.c:166-195 (expiry 176-182, tm_max 183-184, returns 186-194). Reviewer round 1 right (NULL expire result skips the update and tm_max); round 15 right (with rat_update NULL rat_tm becomes now plus the old deadline, line 181).

name: main
prose: Entry point of spi (usr.sbin/spi/spi.c:158-379; slice cut the head). err starts at 0 and is the return value. It sets defaults and parses options (-d device, -f device, -m mode 0..3, -s speed, -c count, -C command bytes (a repeated -C or a bad byte string sets err), -A, -b, -L, -v, -i, -h); the option loop stops at the first error (err = 1) or for -h, where it prints the usage and jumps to the end with err 0. After parsing: if err is set it prints the usage and goes to the end (returning 1); if no direction, info, mode, speed or count was requested it prints the usage and goes to the end with err still 0, so it returns 0 in that case. If a count or command bytes were given without a direction the direction defaults to write (count 0) or read/write; a negative count when not writing prints a message, sets err = 1, prints the usage and ends. With no device name it uses DEFAULT_DEVICE_NAME (a missing name is not an error). It opens the device O_RDWR; on failure it prints an error and returns 1 at the end. With -i it returns get_info's result. Otherwise it applies the mode and speed (set_mode and set_speed results are returned if non-zero, stopping there) and runs perform_read, perform_write or perform_readwrite for the chosen direction, storing its result in err. At the end label it closes the device if it was opened, frees opt.pcmd and returns err.

name: at_cmd
prose: Sends an AT command and waits for its reply (usr.sbin/uhsoctl/uhsoctl.c:580-668). It formats cf with its arguments into a 64-byte buffer cmd (truncated to 63 characters) and writes strlen(cmd) bytes to ctx->fd; if write returns <= 0 it returns -1 at once (no watchdog was started). Otherwise it loops: it zeroes buf, calls watchdog_reset(ctx, 5) and select()s on ctx->fd, repeating the select while it returns <= 0 with errno EINTR; inside that loop, if FLG_WDEXP is set after a select it calls watchdog_disable and returns -2. After the select loop it calls watchdog_disable, so the watchdog is disabled once per reply line (not after each EINTR retry), and every return after the write is preceded by a disable. If select returned <= 0 or readline() returns <= 0 it returns -2. Empty lines and lines that are an echo of the command (strncasecmp of cmd with buf over strlen(buf) characters) are skipped. Any other line is stripped of CR/LF and passed to cb(ra, cmd, buf) if cb is non-NULL. A line starting with "OK" ends the loop with retval kept as it was (0 unless an earlier line left a non-zero retval); a line containing "ERROR" ends it with -1; for other lines, if resp is non-NULL, retval is set to strncmp(buf, resp, strlen(resp)) for that line (so the last such comparison decides the result). It returns retval: 0 on success, -1 for ERROR or a write failure, -2 on watchdog expiry or select/read failure, or the non-zero strncmp value when the OK line followed a non-matching line.

Reviewer round 2 right (no watchdog before the early -1); round 15 right (the watchdog is disabled after the select loop, not after every EINTR retry).

name: voss_httpd_start
prose: Real name voss_httpd_start (usr.sbin/virtual_oss/virtual_oss/httpd.c:776-846; the slice is its body and the packet called it http_server_setup). It returns NULL on success and an error string on failure. If pvp->http.host or port is NULL or nstate is 0 it returns NULL immediately (HTTP disabled). Otherwise it mallocs http.state with nstate entries; failure returns "Could not allocate HTTP states" (no state exists then). It sets each entry's fd to -1 and ts to 0, then allocates a client with vclient_alloc (failure: returns an error string, with the state array left allocated), sets the client's profile and, if rtp_ifname is set, returns an error string when the client's channel count is above 2 (the client is not freed on this or on the next failure), binds the RTP socket with voss_httpd_bind_rtp (a non-NULL result is returned as the error), and sets up buffers for 44.1 kHz 16-bit audio; without RTP it sets http.rtp_fd to -1 and sets up buffers with the default WAV-header format and voss_dsp_sample_rate. If vclient_setup_buffers fails it frees the client with vclient_free and returns an error string. Otherwise it sets rx_enabled = 1 and type VTYPE_OSS_DAT, appends the client to pvp->head under atomic_lock, and creates the server and streamer threads (each pthread_create failure returns an error string; the client stays registered on the list). On success it returns NULL. The state array is never freed here.

name: rpc_received
prose: Records a reply from an NIS server for a domain (usr.sbin/ypbind/ypbind.c:825-971; returns nothing). It returns at once if dom is NULL. It searches ypbindlist for the domain (remembering the previous node). If an entry exists and force is set and it has a broadcast child, it kills that child with SIGINT, closes the read end and clears its descriptors. In secure mode, if the reply port is not below IPPORT_RESERVED it logs a rejection, clears dom_broadcast_pid and dom_alive of an existing entry and returns. If the reply address is zero it switches on ypdb->dom_default, dereferencing ypdb without checking it, so a zero address with no matching entry crashes: for a non-default entry it unlinks it from the list, closes its lock descriptor, unlinks its binding file, frees it, decrements domains and returns; for a default entry (value 1) it clears dom_broadcast_pid and dom_alive, calls broadcast(ypdb) and returns; other values fall through. If no entry exists, it returns when force is 0, when the domain name is longer than YPMAXDOMAIN (logged), or when malloc fails; otherwise it creates a zeroed entry for the domain and pushes it on the list. It then logs 'OK' after a recovered outage, copies the server address into the entry, sets dom_vers to YPVERS, dom_alive to 1 and dom_broadcast_pid to 0, and closes the old lock descriptor if one was set (without resetting dom_lockfd). It creates the binding file <BINDINGDIR>/<domain>.<version> with a shared lock (retrying once after mkdir BINDINGDIR); if both opens fail it returns with the in-memory entry updated but dom_lockfd still holding the old, already closed descriptor and no binding file. Otherwise it stores the new descriptor in dom_lockfd and writes the port and a success reply (server address and port) with writev; if the write is short or fails it logs, closes the descriptor, sets dom_lockfd to -1 and returns.

Reviewer round 1 right (open/write failures leave the entry recorded without a binding file); round 15 right (a zero address with no matching entry dereferences NULL at line 868).

name: ber_write_elements
prose: Real name ber_write_elements (usr.sbin/ypldap/ber.c:761-791; the packet slice 766-1018 also contains other functions). It computes len = ber_calc_len(root), which also rewrites be_len of sequence and set elements in the tree and returns 0 for an empty EOC element. If the write buffer ber->br_wbuf exists and br_wbuf + len would pass br_wend, it frees it and sets it to NULL (br_wend is left unchanged); a buffer that is large enough is reused. If br_wbuf is NULL it mallocs len bytes (a failure returns -1 with br_wbuf NULL) and sets br_wend to the end. It resets br_wptr to br_wbuf and calls ber_dump_element(ber, root); a failure returns -1 (the buffer stays allocated and br_wptr stays wherever the dump left it). On success, if ber->fd != -1 it returns write(ber->fd, br_wbuf, len), which may be -1 or fewer than len; otherwise it returns len. The buffer stays owned by *ber for reuse. For an element tree whose computed length is 0 (an empty EOC element) the buffer is allocated with size 0 and what ber_dump_element writes for it was not read, so the claim that the buffer holds the full encoding is only established for non-empty trees.

name: main
prose: Entry point of yppush (usr.sbin/yppush/yppush_main.c:492-633; slice cut the head; hostlist is a local variable). It parses -d domain, -j jobs (values <= 0 become 1), -p yp_dir, -h host (pushed onto a local list; a malloc failure calls yp_error and yppush_exit(1)), -t timeout and -v; any other option calls usage(). If no map name follows it calls usage(). If no domain was given: when yp_get_default_domain succeeds and _yp_check reports NIS not running it prints 'no domain specified and NIS not running' and calls usage(); in the other cases (including yp_get_default_domain failing) it just calls yp_get_default_domain again to set yppush_domain and continues, possibly leaving it NULL. It reads the local host name (gethostname failure: yp_error and yppush_exit(1)) and the YP_MASTER_NAME record of the map with yp_get_record (anything but YP_TRUE: yp_error and yppush_exit(1)). If the local name matches the master name (strncasecmp over the record length) and no host list was given, skip_master is set; if it does not match, it only prints 'warning: this host is not the master' (and exits 1 when NITPICKY is defined). It copies the master name into a freshly malloc'ed yppush_master (the malloc result is not checked), installs the SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers and sets yppush_transid to the current time. With a host list it calls yppush_foreach once per listed host; otherwise it runs ypxfr_get_map on the ypservers map from localhost with yppush_foreach as the callback. With -v 2 or more it reports that all jobs were dispatched, and it ends with yppush_exit(0) (exit(0) afterwards as a fallback). main does not return.
note: usr.sbin/yppush/yppush_main.c:492-633 (getopt 504-536, mapname 541-546, domain 552-560 (condition at 554-555), master 564-596, dispatch 605-623, exit 629-632). Reviewer round 15 right: usage() is only called when yp_get_default_domain succeeds and _yp_check fails; if yp_get_default_domain fails it continues. Being a non-master is only a warning without NITPICKY.

name: parse_config_file
prose: Parses the nscd configuration file fname into config (usr.sbin/nscd/parser.c:368-553). The asserts check config and fname are non-NULL. If fopen fails it returns -1 without touching *error_str or *error_line. Otherwise it reads the file with fgets into a 255-byte buffer (longer lines arrive as several pieces, each counted as a line), splits each into fields with strbreak and, until the first error, dispatches on the first field: blank lines and '#' comments are skipped. Valid forms and their effect: enable-cache NAME yes/no (enable_cache), debug-level 0..10 (recognised and accepted, including out-of-range values because get_number returns -2 which is not -1; it is not applied to config), positive-time-to-live, positive-confidence-threshold, negative-time-to-live, negative-confidence-threshold and suggested-size (a value <= 0 sets invalid_value and counts as an error), positive-policy and negative-policy (fifo/lru/lfu), perform-actual-lookups yes/no, keep-hot-count (a negative value is an error), threads N (set_threads_num is called with get_number's result, which is -2 for N < 1), and check-files NAME yes/no (the called check_files function does nothing). Any line that is not one of these valid forms is an error: the function logs it, sets *error_str to "invalid value" if invalid_value was set by an out-of-range value of one of the checked directives, otherwise to "syntax error", sets *error_line to the line number, sets the result to -1 and stops reading. The file is closed and the function returns 0 if every line was accepted, or -1 after an error.
note: usr.sbin/nscd/parser.c:368-553 (fopen 382-386, loop 392-548, error text 536-547); get_number 313-331 (returns -2 when out of range), check_files 291-298 is a no-op. Reviewer round 1 right (out-of-range debug-level and threads values are accepted, threads gets -2); round 2 right (debug-level is ignored, not applied); round 15 right (check-files is a no-op).
